data.title: Add docket ready command
data.body:
## Goal

Add a `docket ready` command that shows the highest priority approved bug ready for work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docket ready` shows the single highest priority Approved bug
- [ ] Priority ordering: High > Medium > Low
- [ ] Within same priority, oldest (first created) wins
- [ ] `docket ready -n 5` or `docket ready --count 5` shows top N bugs
- [ ] Output includes ID, priority, title, and age
- [ ] If no approved bugs exist, show helpful message
- [ ] Consider: `docket ready --work` to immediately start work on top bug

## Context

Answers the question "what should I work on next?" without having to scan through `docket list --status approved` and mentally sort by priority.

Example output:
```
$ docket ready
Ready to work: abc1 (High) - Add user authentication
  Created 3 days ago

$ docket ready -n 3
1. abc1 (High) - Add user authentication (3 days)
2. def2 (High) - Fix payment bug (1 day)
3. ghi3 (Medium) - Update docs (5 days)
```

The `--work` flag would be a nice shortcut:
```
$ docket ready --work
# Equivalent to: docket work $(docket ready --quiet)
```
